independent_variables.name: Post
independent_variables.definition: An indicator equal to 1 if the rule was written after Business Roundtable v. SEC (March 2012 and onward), and 0 if written before.

evidence.quote: An indicator that is equal to 1 if the rule was written after _Business_ _Roundtable v. SEC_ (i.e., March 2012 and onward), and 0 if the rule was written before

independent_variables.name: Final
independent_variables.definition: An indicator equal to 1 if a document is a final rule release, and 0 if it is a proposed rule release.

review_notes: Principal baseline selected independently as Section 5.2.1 / Table 4, the authors’ Hypothesis 1 test of whether Business Roundtable v. SEC is associated with increased academic citations in proposed or final rules. The equation uses OLS with Post, Final, their interaction, and the full control set. Two separate baseline models retain the distinct citation-presence and citation-count outcomes. Columns (3) and (6) are selected because they are the final full-control columns after controls enter stepwise. Table 5 tests the distinct Hypothesis 2 citation-tone outcome, while Section 5.3 tests downstream lobbying outcomes; these are follow-up questions rather than the principal citation-number family.
descriptive_reason: Table 3 reports distributions for Cite_dum, Cite_N, Mandatory and Word Count by release type. It provides no descriptive moments for Post, Final or Post*Final; Word Count is retained as the raw version for DocLength because no logged DocLength moments are reported.
results_review_notes: The principal family is Table 4 Hypothesis 1; full-control columns (3) and (6) retained for the separate citation-presence and citation-count outcomes.
